## General

- POLICY: Job Breakdown Usage for analysis: The Job breakdown should be used as a reference for how many hours are required for any piece of the job, so that we can determine roughly the best crew size and duration of days needed to complete that part of the job.

## Crews & Staffing

- POLICY: Never split framing: Framing is never split between a sub and the in-house crew.

## Scheduling

- POLICY: No demo without materials: Never demo without the next phase's materials on site, and never schedule a job before the customer's final material selections are made.
- POLICY: Interior trade concurrency: No more than two trades work concurrently inside the building; exterior trades carry no such limit.

- POLICY: Mobilization floor: No mobilized trade task is sized below 4 crew-hours — showing up, setting up, and closing out is real work.
- POLICY: Rate card governs: Task sizing anchors to the production-rate card; deviate only on job-specific evidence (access, choppy layout, occupied home) and cite the deviation in the basis.
    Notes: Seeded 2026-09-14 from convergent foreman calibration on Pawnee tests 5-8. Correct any number and future schedules obey it.
- POLICY: Elevated / second-story access premium: Second-story or elevated work carries an access premium: +20-25% on demo, framing, siding, and window labor hours (scaffold moves, hoisting, debris lowering); scaffold erect/strike is billed explicitly (~4-8 crew-hours per mobilization); material handling through an occupied home is real hours, never free.
    Notes: Seeded 2026-09-14 from the Crawford audit: ground-calibrated card rates under-priced elevated work until the foreman caught it ad-hoc. Correct the percentage and future schedules obey.

## Inbox

- POLICY: Never ask about season or weather timing: Never ask questions about season, weather, or winter timing. The job's scheduled start date is authoritative and seasonal feasibility is the PM's call — plan from the start date as given.

## Proposed (machine-derived, UNVETTED — canon above wins on any conflict)

- POLICY: 3D design presentation sets are visualization-only; the proposal governs scope and field measurement governs dimensions: Customer-signed 3D design presentation sets carry a disclaimer that drawings are for general visualization and structural reference only, dimensions are approximate, field measurements govern, and rendered colors/materials are not selections; where a presentation set shows dimensions, finishes, or elements that differ from the proposal, the proposal defines contracted scope and the difference is logged as an open conflict for the PM rather than adopted into the plan. (Unvetted, Confidence 60% → General)
- POLICY: Demolished ceiling assemblies require an explicit ceiling rebuild scope before insulation and drywall tasks are generated: When a scope demolishes existing ceiling assemblies but finishes 'walls only', the ceiling rebuild (roof-cavity insulation, venting or unvented strategy, ceiling finish) is treated as an open scope gap that the PM settles before insulation/drywall tasks are generated; the plan never leaves a conditioned room with an open rafter cavity by silent default. (Unvetted, Confidence 60% → Structure & Site)
- POLICY: Drywall on an existing masonry wall carries a furring or framed-wall task and a moisture strategy: Where drywall is specified over an existing brick or block wall, the plan carries an explicit furring-strip or framed-wall task (with any insulation and vapor control decided) ahead of the drywall hang; drywall square footage on a masonry wall is never sized as if it were on framed studs. (Unvetted, Confidence 55% → Structure & Site)
